introH2: 🏝️ What kind of stays does Koh Lanta in Krabi have, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: Koh Lanta is Krabi's long Andaman-coast island, known for a laid-back mood — more relaxing than partying, with beaches strung one after another and sunsets people come back for · what many don't realise is that Koh Lanta is reached by car, no passenger boat like Phi Phi — take a car or minivan from town or Krabi Airport, about 2–2.5 hrs, cross on a short car ferry or use the Siri Lanta Bridge, then drive straight up to your stay · the island's beaches run clearly from north to south — the north (Klong Dao, Long Beach/Phra Ae) is near the pier, with plenty of shops, good for families, while the south (Klong Nin, Klong Toab, Kantiang Bay, Klong Jark) gets quieter and more luxurious the further down you go, but also further out, so you'll want a car or motorbike · we've ranked this list by real guest review scores, rounding up 9 Koh Lanta stays we've reviewed in depth, giving both the good points and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites with direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Koh Lanta is reached by car, no passenger boat like Phi Phi — take a car/minivan from Krabi town or Krabi Airport (~2–2.5 hrs), cross on a short car ferry, or use the Siri Lanta Bridge from Koh Lanta Noi to Koh Lanta Yai · the beaches run from north to south: Klong Dao (near Saladan Pier, quiet/family) · Long Beach–Phra Ae (long, plenty of shops) · Klong Khong–Klong Nin–Klong Toab (west coast, quiet, good for sunsets) · Kantiang Bay (luxury, remote) · Klong Jark (the quietest) — the further south, the further out, so you'll want a car/motorbike to get around · ⚠️ many resorts close in the rainy season, May–October, so check before booking.

faqTitle: FAQ — questions travellers often ask about staying on Koh Lanta, Krabi

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to Koh Lanta, do you have to take a boat?
faq.a: No passenger boat like Koh Phi Phi · Koh Lanta is reached by car, taking a car or minivan from Krabi town or Krabi Airport, about 2–2.5 hrs · to cross from Lanta Noi to Lanta Yai there's either a short car ferry (it carries vehicles) or the now-open Siri Lanta Bridge, so you can drive straight up to your stay · we recommend renting a car or motorbike to get around, especially if you're staying on a south-side beach that's further out

faq.q: ❓ Which beach on Koh Lanta should I stay at, family or couples?
faq.a: The beaches run clearly from north to south · the north — Klong Dao and Long Beach (Phra Ae) is near Saladan Pier, with plenty of shops, easy to get around, good for families and short trips, like Southern Lanta, Lanta Castaway, Layana and Avani+ · the south — Klong Nin, Klong Toab, Kantiang Bay, Klong Jark gets quieter and more luxurious the further down you go, but further out, good for couples and relaxers who want privacy, like SriLanta, Rawi Warin, Pimalai, The Houben and Klong Jark · on the south side you'll want a car/motorbike to get out for food

faq.q: ❓ When is the best time for Koh Lanta, and do resorts really close in the rainy season?
faq.a: The best time is high season, November–April, calm seas, fine weather and clear water, good for swimming and sunsets, but prices are high and rooms fill fast, so book ahead · during May–October (low season/rainy season) there's more rain and stronger waves, prices drop and there are fewer people, but many resorts on the island close over the rainy season, especially the remote south side, so check with the stay before planning and before every booking

faq.q: ❓ Does Koh Lanta have both luxury and light-budget stays?
faq.a: It has both · the most luxurious is Pimalai (Small Luxury Hotels of the World, ฿6,500) and adults-only Layana (฿6,500), at Kantiang Bay and Long Beach · for great-value luxury there's Rawi Warin ฿2,600 (5-star on the hillside) and The Houben ฿3,900 (an adults-only clifftop boutique) · and there are still plenty of light-budget options, like Lanta Castaway ฿1,100, Southern Lanta ฿1,100 and Klong Jark ฿1,200 · choose by budget and check the real reviews before booking

faq.q: ❓ Do you need to rent a car/motorbike to stay on Koh Lanta?
faq.a: It depends on the beach · if you stay on the north side (Klong Dao/Long Beach) near the pier and the village, you can walk to food and shops, so you may not need a vehicle · but if you stay on the south side (Klong Nin, Klong Toab, Kantiang Bay, Klong Jark), which gets further out and quieter the lower you go, you should rent a car or motorbike to get out for food, visit other beaches and catch sunsets at different spots, since shops are spread out and public transport on the island is limited · some luxury resorts have a shuttle, so check when booking
